task.name: forge post-merge cleanup fast-forwards the operator's checkout to origin/base_branch, silently corrupting a checked-out release branch
task.story_text:
## Observed

During a release-line sprint — operator checkout sitting on `release/v0.13`, `workspace.base_branch` = `main` — each story's PR merges to `main`, and forge's post-merge local cleanup then runs, in the operator's project-root checkout:

```
git fetch origin
git merge --ff-only origin/main
```

Because the checked-out branch (`release/v0.13`) was an ancestor of `origin/main`, the `--ff-only` merge succeeds and fast-forwards `release/v0.13` up to `origin/main`, silently importing main's dev version (`pyproject.toml` becomes `0.12.0.dev0`, replacing `0.13.0rc2`), main's `[Unreleased]` CHANGELOG section, and main's forward-port merge commits. Over one three-story sprint this fired three times with no operator-visible signal (the step is wrapped in `try/except` and logged only as "non-fatal"). The release branch was left content-identical to main; an rc cut from it would have shipped main's version string and history.

## Diagnosis

- **Observed symptom:** a sprint run from a release-branch checkout leaves that release branch fast-forwarded to `origin/main` — wrong version file, wrong changelog, and main-only merge commits in its history — with no error surfaced to the operator.
- **Evidence:** `src/theforge/coordinator/completion.py` (~L856–871), the "best-effort local cleanup after a successful remote PR merge" step, runs `git merge --ff-only origin/{base_branch}` with `cwd=project_root`. `base_branch` resolves from `config.workspace.base_branch`, which is `main`. The project-root checkout was on `release/v0.13`, an ancestor of `origin/main`, so the fast-forward succeeded and advanced `release/v0.13`. The branch reflog shows three `merge origin/main: Fast-forward` entries during the sprint; afterward `git show release/v0.13:pyproject.toml` read `0.12.0.dev0` (main's version) instead of `0.13.0rc2`.
- **Ruled out:** the release/rc tooling. `scripts/cut-rc.sh` only fast-forwards the *release* branch to its own origin ref (`git pull --ff-only origin <release-branch>`) and creates from main solely when the branch does not yet exist; it never merges main into an existing release branch. No script in the repository runs `git merge origin/main`.
- **Confirmed cause:** the post-merge cleanup assumes the operator's checked-out branch is the base branch and fast-forwards it to `origin/{base_branch}` unconditionally. When those two differ — dogfooding a release line while `base_branch` is still `main` — it advances the wrong branch. The mismatch is reachable by construction, not just by operator error: `base_branch` is a single global config value with no relationship to the branch actually checked out.
- **Affected code path:** `src/theforge/coordinator/completion.py` post-merge local cleanup (`git merge --ff-only origin/{base_branch}` at ~L865, `cwd=project_root`); `config.workspace.base_branch` resolution feeding it.
- **Fix-success criterion:** after a sprint whose base branch differs from the operator's checked-out branch, that checkout's tip, tracked files (version, changelog), and history are unchanged by forge — no branch other than the intended base is advanced, and any inability to sync the base is surfaced rather than silently mutating a different branch.

## Expected

A tool that lands work onto a base branch must never mutate the operator's currently checked-out branch as a side effect of that landing. A convenience step that syncs the local base branch has to first establish that the checked-out branch actually is the base branch; when it is not, it must leave the checkout untouched rather than fast-forwarding it to the base's tip. Advancing a branch to another branch's tip changes that branch's identity — its version files, its changelog, the set of commits it contains — so it cannot be treated as a best-effort convenience whose failure is swallowed and unlogged; silently rewriting which commits a release line carries is corruption, not cleanup. Where the branch a tool operates on and the branch it treats as the base can legitimately differ, the base must be derived from or checked against the working context rather than read from a single global setting that may not match what is checked out.

handoff.summary: Guarded post-merge local base sync so forge first resolves the checked-out branch in the operator's project-root checkout and only runs `git fetch origin` plus `git merge --ff-only origin/<base>` when that branch exactly matches the configured base branch. When the checkout differs or cannot be identified, forge now leaves it untouched and emits an operator-visible warning. Added merge-path regression tests covering both the allowed fast-forward-on-base case and the skip-with-warning case for a mismatched release checkout.

commits.message: fix(coordinator): guard post-merge base sync by checkout branch

acceptance_criteria.criterion: post-merge cleanup must not fast-forward the operator's checkout when it is not the base branch
acceptance_criteria.notes: Cleanup now probes `git symbolic-ref --short HEAD` in `project_root` and skips the local base fast-forward unless the checked-out branch exactly matches `workspace.base_branch`; regression coverage asserts no fetch/merge occurs on `release/v0.13` while other cleanup still runs.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: failure/mismatch must be surfaced rather than silently swallowed
acceptance_criteria.notes: Branch mismatch or unknown branch state now emits an operator-visible `_log` warning and a structured warning log instead of silently mutating the checkout.

reviews.summary: [openai-gpt-5.5] The release-branch corruption path is guarded, but failed base syncs are still silently ignored. | [claude-opus] Post-merge base sync is now gated on the checked-out branch matching the configured base; mismatch and unknown-branch cases are surfaced, and regression tests reproduce the original release-branch corruption scenario.

findings.description: When the operator checkout is on the configured base branch and either the fetch or ff-only merge exits nonzero, cleanup proceeds without any operator-visible warning or structured failure log.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
